metadata.notes: CUT-shaped (data/actions/cut.json): one verb with a 'fineness' parameter rather than two, since coarse-vs-paste is a difference of degree, not of kind. The generic mash/crush verb potato.json's metadata flagged as missing since the very first potato entity ('mash isn't wired up yet') — implemented here for garlic first, where it's load-bearing (see emulsify.json's statePrerequisite), not retrofitted onto potato speculatively. Mortar-specific, not mixer/blender-based — see mortar.json.
metadata.finenessNote: 'cracked'/'ground' added 2026-08-13 for black_pepper.json (whole peppercorns crushed to cracked or ground, the real distinction behind 'freshly cracked black pepper' vs. table-ground — coarse/fine_paste don't fit a dry spice that never becomes a paste). Kept as ONE shared enum on the existing verb rather than a second fineness parameter or a new verb: garlic and pepper both answer the same real question ('how finely was this crushed'), just with different endpoint vocabulary for their respective materials — same reasoning CUT's single 'shape' enum already applies across every choppable entity in this repo, not just potato.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true — further crushing an already-crushed target is physically continuous (coarse -> fine_paste is a spectrum), not a discrete duplication risk.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): repeated pounding/grinding toward a tactile-force threshold (verification.method is literally tactile_force: 'resistance drops to near-zero and texture matches the requested fineness') — an accumulating, sensor-terminated process, the same shape as mash.json. DISAGREES with the engine's test (applyAction one-shot). Classified continuous per TICKET 1's rule.

verification.description: Resistance drops to near-zero and texture matches the requested fineness (coarse vs. fine_paste)

hazards.note: Mortar and pestle — minor pinch/impact risk
